s1.syndrome_frame: Rapidly progressive gait disturbance with spinal cord compression
salient_findings: Decreased sensation from T3 dermatome downward
Clonus and hyperreflexia in lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Diffusely enhancing lesion on thoracic spine MRI with cord compression
Expansile bony lesion of T1 vertebral body on CT
key_facts: 1-week history of rapidly progressive gait disturbance
No back pain, fevers, night sweats, or weight loss
No history of smoking or known malignancy
Full strength throughout all extremities
Decreased sensation from T3 dermatome downward
Four beats of clonus bilaterally
Hyperreflexia in lower extremities
Profound ataxia
Unable to walk more than a few steps
Diffusely enhancing lesion on thoracic spine MRI
Severe cord compression on MRI
Expansile bony lesion of T1 vertebral body on CT
No evidence of primary malignancy on CT scans of chest, abdomen, and pelvis
Laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, within normal limits

shortlist.label: Chordoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion of T1 vertebral body with extension into posterior elements, consistent with chordoma

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma
shortlist.why_kept: Diffusely enhancing lesion on thoracic spine MRI with severe cord compression, possible myeloma involvement

shortlist.label: Metastatic lung cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression, possible metastatic disease

shortlist.label: Plasmacytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary expansile bony lesion with diffuse enhancement, possible plasmacytoma

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of neurological symptoms with spinal cord compression, possible lymphoma involvement

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile bony lesion with aggressive features, possible osteosarcoma

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rapidly progressive neurological decline with spinal cord compression, possible Ewing's sarcoma

shortlist.label: Spinal metastasis from unknown primary
shortlist.why_kept: Severe cord compression with unknown primary malignancy, possible metastatic disease

raw.rationale: The presence of a diffusely enhancing lesion with near-circumferential epidural extension and an expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body, along with the absence of a primary malignancy, is most consistent with a chordoma, which is a rare, slow-growing tumor that can cause spinal cord compression and neurological decline.

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms such as bone pain, fevers, and weight loss, which are absent in this case

rejected.label: Metastatic lung cancer
rejected.why: Patient has no history of smoking or known malignancy, and CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed no evidence of a primary malignancy

rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with a solitary lesion and systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Typically presents with systemic symptoms and lymphadenopathy, which are absent in this case

rejected.label: Osteosarcoma
rejected.why: Usually presents in younger patients and is associated with a more aggressive clinical course

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: Typically presents in younger patients and is associated with systemic symptoms and a more aggressive clinical course

rejected.label: Spinal metastasis from unknown primary
rejected.why: The absence of a primary malignancy on CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis makes this diagnosis less likely
